pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

## What

Flips the machine-loop factory pin in lockstep (`machine-sm.yml` + `ai-teammate.yml`, guarded by `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` — 6/6 green):

## Why

The factory checks out `factory-agents/` at EXACTLY the pinned ref — the rework leg's `postJSAction` (`factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js`) has been running **pre-fix** code: a rework CLI command dying with a non-zero exit was announced as `✅ Rework Complete` (the error text rode INSIDE the posted summary). - **#568** — mergeBot: `workspace/repository` args for `github_get_commit_check_runs` (merge leg crashed with `Required parameter 'workspace' is missing`).
- **#558** (from the superseded main-side flip) — git-guard double-shim exec-loop fix.
- **#566** — pack-registry runner overrides; agent-pack release cut on top.

## Gates

- `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart`: 6/6.
- Conflict with main resolved (pin-vs-pin; took the superset side).

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
    with:
      factory_ref: 1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

...
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @171b9398 — ships #569
    # (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no longer announced as "Rework
    # Complete" — the #1052 loop) + #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository
    # args) + #566 (pack-registry runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}...

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

## PR Description

## What this flips

All three machine-loop stubs (ai-teammate.yml, machine-sm.yml, machine-merge.yml) move from dmtools-agents `08a874dd` to **`20c10eee191fd56e447cf7f1b67b83c4db46dfd2`** — `uses:` + `factory_ref:` in lockstep (4 pin occurrences per stub pair, 6 total plus the in-file comment).

## What the new pin ships (dmtools-agents @ 20c10eee)

| PR | Change | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| #569 | A fatal rework CLI exit is **no longer reported as completion** | the feedback loop sees the failure and re-dispatches instead of posting "Rework Completed" on a dead run |
| #570 | `sm_github.json: maxTriggeredWorkflows 1 → 3` | the per-tick workflow **budget** stops starving review/validate legs when one long machine-loop run holds the single slot (live 2026-09-29: every leg skipped "global workflow cap reached: 1" for hours; gh-1078/gh-1083 dev handoffs skipped) |
| #571 | factory teammate leg **self-heals a broken dmtools install** | probe (`command -v` + `$HOME/.dmtools/bin`) + `dmtools --version` + forced reinstall of the pinned bundle before `dmtools run` |
| #572 | SM rule `review-stale-verdict-unchecked` | a **validated+reviewed** PR whose head lost its checks (push moved it after the review) gets a **re-REVIEW first** (owner rule 2026-09-29); the single pre-merge validation stays in `validate-armed` (post-approve, final head). Closes the chicken-and-egg stall (live: pr-1076/pr-1075 — every review path required `checks=green`, tick processed 0 until a human label) |

## Scope (4 files)

- `.github/workflows/ai-teammate.yml` — pin flip only
- `.github/workflows/machine-sm.yml` — pin flip + in-file comment
- `.github/workflows/machine-merge.yml` — pin flip (kept in lockstep)

## Gates

- `factory_stub_ref_test.dart`: **7/7 green** (immutable-SHA, three-stub lockstep, factory_ref echo ×3, explicit secrets ×3 + no `secrets: inherit` ×3, assignment gate, dispatch-reachability, no PR trigger)
- Full Dart suite green; YAML parses (actionlint)

- Round 1: 🚨 BLOCKING — #1017/#544 concurrency fix lost in the rebase → restored (`pr-{0}` fallback + run-name guard)
- Round 2: 🚨 BLOCKING — merge stub skew → machine-merge.yml pinned + third-stub lockstep guard added

## Gates

- `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart`: 6/6.
- Conflict with main resolved (pin-vs-pin; took the superset side).

    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
    with:
      factory_ref: 1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

...
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. ## PR Description

## What

Flips the machine-loop factory pin in lockstep (`machine-sm.yml` + `ai-teammate.yml`, guarded by `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart` — 6/6 green):

```
- uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-{sm,teammate}.yml@6b953f80…  (#477)
+ uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-{sm,teammate}.yml@171b9392…  (dmtools-agents main)
```

Rebased on main: supersedes the intermediate `1fdb4c6c` (#558) flip — **171b9392 is a strict superset of it** (#558 + 13 commits, incl. both fixes below), so nothing from the main-side flip is lost.

## Why

The factory checks out `factory-agents/` at EXACTLY the pinned ref — the rework leg's `postJSAction` (`factory-agents/js/pushReworkChanges.js`) has been running **pre-fix** code: a rework CLI command dying with a non-zero exit was announced as `✅ Rework Complete` (the error text rode INSIDE the posted summary). Live consequence — the #1052 loop: ~7 rework rounds in 12h, each 'Rework finished' → deterministic red validation → rework re-queued, forever.

## What the new pin ships (dmtools-agents @ 171b9392)

- **#569** — rework: fatal CLI failure (`Error: Command failed (exit code N≠0,≠124)`) → one resume attempt, then ❌ + ticket back to In Rework + `success:false`. Never a completion announcement.
- **#568** — mergeBot: `workspace/repository` args for `github_get_commit_check_runs` (merge leg crashed with `Required parameter 'workspace' is missing`).
- **#558** (from the superseded main-side flip) — git-guard double-shim exec-loop fix.
- **#566** — pack-registry runner overrides; agent-pack release cut on top.

## Gates

- `test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart`: 6/6.
- Conflict with main resolved (pin-vs-pin; took the superset side).

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
    with:
      factory_ref: 1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

blocks.text:
# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ROLLOUT SCOPE (this phase): the loop reacts ONLY to artifacts authored
# by the machine itself — issues opened by `ai-teammate` and PRs opened
# by `ai-teammate`. Human-created issues (even labeled/assigned to the
# agent) do NOT trigger anything yet; that gate opens in a later phase.
#
#   issue ASSIGNED to ai-teammate   → factory, leg=dev (fresh handoff)
#   issue labeled while assigned     → factory, leg derived by the guard
#   PR opened by ai-teammate         → factory, leg=review on the linked
#                                      issue (parsed from the PR body)
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual)  → leg pinned by input
#
# ALL loop logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/
# factory-teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file
# carries only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository
# event triggers, the author filter, the PR→issue resolution, the
# per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      (github.event.inputs.pr != '' &&
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · pr-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.pr) ||
       format('▶ {0} (SM) · gh-{1}', github.event.inputs.leg, github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      format('{0} · gh-{1}: {2}',
        github.event.action == 'assigned' && '⚒️ dev (assigned handoff)' || 'machine loop',
        github.event.issue.number, github.event.issue.title) }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

...
    outputs:
      issue: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ steps.resolve.outputs.leg }}
    steps:
      - name: Resolve target issue and leg for this event
        id: resolve
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          ACTION: ${{ github.event.action }}
          NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          case "$EVENT" in
            workflow_dispatch)
              # Manual/SM dispatch: inputs flow straight through.
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"   # empty here; factory takes inputs.issue
              echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
            issues)
              # Assignment-driven loop: a fresh `assigned` event (human
              # handoff) → dev leg; `labeled` (agent:review / agent:rework
              # added by the machine itself while assigned) → guard derives.
              # POLICY (#693 steering): dev fires ONLY when ai-teammate is
              # the sole assignee — any human assignee owns the issue and
              # the machine stands by for reviews instead (review paths:
              # review-external-once / agent:review on the eventual PR).
              if [ "$ACTION" = "assigned" ]; then
                HUMAN=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${ISSUE_NUMBER}" \
                  --jq '[.assignees[].login] | map(select(. != "ai-teammate")) | length')
                if [ "$HUMAN" = "0" ]; then
                  echo "leg=dev" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                else
                  echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
                  echo "::notice title=machine-standby::issue #${ISSUE_NUMBER} has a human assignee — no dev, review-only"
                fi
              else
                echo "leg=" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              fi
              echo "issue=${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              ;;
          esac
          echo "→ gate done (see outputs)"

  factory:
    needs: gate
    # Dispatch runs carry the target in inputs (gate outputs are empty by
    # design there); event runs carry it in gate outputs.
    if: needs.gate.result == 'success' && (needs.gate.outputs.issue != '' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')
    # Job-scoped grants mirroring the pinned callee's declared scopes (a
    # reusable call is capped by the calling job's effective permissions —
    # see the top-level comment). Scoped to THIS job so any future job in
    # this workflow defaults to the top-level read-only.
    permissions:
      contents: write         # the factory pushes branches / session trees
      issues: write           # labels, comments, close-issue safety net
      pull-requests: write    # PR creation, review threads, update-branch
      actions: write          # actions/cache save phase + workflow_dispatch
    # Pinned to an immutable SHA of IstiN/dmtools-agents (branch heads move;
    # a branch ref executes whatever is at the head at run start). Flip in
    # lockstep with the machine-sm.yml pin — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
      # STRING — number/choice-typed reusable inputs cannot take expressions.
      issue: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.issue || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      # #687: PR-anchored review (SM dispatches with pr instead of issue).
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      # #687: machine login via jobParams — branch-independent (the
      # checked-out PR branch carries no machineAuthor config).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      leg: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.leg || github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'ai-teammate-author gate' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect on dmtools-dart: inherit => startup failure).

# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents main @171b9398 — ships #569
    # (rework: a fatal CLI failure is no longer announced as "Rework
    # Complete" — the #1052 loop) + #568 (mergeBot workspace/repository
    # args) + #566 (pack-registry runner overrides).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 171b9398c7df7b55cfa0c55644332da3bc6f67ff
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}...

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

blocks.text:
# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head
# pushes, check-run completions — and runs the deterministic mergeBot
# (factory-merge.yml) so approved green PRs merge within seconds.
# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
    with:
      factory_ref: 1fdb4c6c5d9d7526c6083fe512baaf7ca571210f
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
